# vcp_vmware_server_public_interface (Resource)

Adds a public address to a VMware Cloud server by attaching an interface on a shared public network.

~> A server already comes with a public interface of its own — that one belongs to `vcp_vmware_server` (`public_network_id` / `network_bandwidth_mbps`) and must not be managed here. This resource is for the **additional** addresses, each of which is charged separately.

~> `bandwidth_mbps` is changed in place; the address family is not, so switching `is_ipv6` replaces the interface and the server gets a different address. Removing an interface from a running server needs an image that supports NIC hot-remove.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An additional public address for a server. The server's first public interface
# is part of vcp_vmware_server (public_network_id / network_bandwidth_mbps) and
# must not be managed here — every interface added by this resource is charged
# separately.
resource "vcp_vmware_server_public_interface" "extra" {
  server_id      = vcp_vmware_server.web.id
  bandwidth_mbps = 100
}

# The platform picks the network and the address; both are readable afterwards.
output "extra_public_ip" {
  value = vcp_vmware_server_public_interface.extra.ip
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bandwidth_mbps` (Number) Bandwidth of the interface in Mbps. Changed in place, and read back from the interface — a change made in the panel shows up as a difference on the next plan.
- `server_id` (Number) ID of the server. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `is_ipv6` (Boolean) Ask for an IPv6 address instead of IPv4. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) ID of the network interface.
- `ip` (String) Public address assigned to the interface.
- `mac` (String) MAC address of the interface.
- `network_id` (Number) ID of the shared public network the platform picked.
- `number` (Number) Position of the interface on the server.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Public interfaces are imported as "<server_id>:<nic_id>" — the ID of the
# network interface, which is listed in the server's `nics` attribute.
terraform import vcp_vmware_server_public_interface.extra 5678:9013
```
